questions.question: The human saliva contains an enzyme called salivary ______ that breaks down starch, a complex molecule, into sugar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Amylase__**__.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Enzyme__**

 __
 
• Enzymes are proteins that act as biological catalysts.
 
• Enzymes increase the reaction rate by lowering its activation energy.
 
• The study of enzymes is called enzymology.
 
 
 
• Amylase__
 __
 
• It is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of starch into sugars.
 
• All amylases are glycoside hydrolases.
 
• alpha and beta amylases are important in brewing beer and liquor made from sugars derived from starch.
 
• Amylases are used in breadmaking and to breakdown complex sugars, such as starch into simple sugars.
 
• Saccharides are a food source rich in energy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Protease

 
 
• A protease is an enzyme that catalyzes proteolysis.
 
• Protease occurs in all organisms from prokaryotes to eukaryotes to viruses.
 
• It is involved in many biological functions, including digestion of ingested proteins, protein catabolism, and cell signaling.
 
• Protease is used to make Paneer.
 
• Proteases are used in industry, medicine, and basic biological research.
 
 
 
• **Lipase**
 
 
• Lipase is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of fats (lipids)
 
• Lipases perform essential roles in digestion transport and processing of dietary lipids.
 
• The main lipases of the human digestive system are pancreatic lipase and pancreatic lipase-related protein 2.
 
• Lipases are a subclass of the esterases.
 
 
 
• **Peptidase**
 
 
• It is an enzyme that breaks down peptides into amino acids.
 
• It is produced in the stomach, small intestine, and pancreas.

questions.question: ______ is defined as the study of the behavior of individual decision-making units such as consumers, resource-owners, and firms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Microeconomics.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Microeconomics**

 
 
• It is the study of decisions made by people and businesses regarding the allocation of resources and prices at which they exchange goods and services.
 
• **Tools of Microeconomics**: Supply and Demand
 
• **Objectives**: It aims to determine the price of a commodity or factors of production
 
• It assumes all the macro variables to be constant i.e. assumes that national income, consumption, savings are constant.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Macroeconomics**

 
 
• It is that part of economic theory which studies the behavior of aggregates of the economy as a whole.
 
• **Tools of Macroeconomics:** Aggregate Supply and Aggregate Demand
 
• **Objectives**: It aims to determine the income and employment level of the economy
 
• It assumes all the micro variables to be constant i.e. decisions of households and firms, prices of individual products are constant.
 
 
 
• **Econometrics**
 
 
• It is the use of statistical methods using quantitative data to create theories or test in economics and finance
 
• Its objectives to provide numerical values to the parameters of economic relationships.
 
 
 
• **Health Economics**
 
 
• It is the part of economics applied to the health care topic.
 
• Its main objectives are to study how scarce resources are allocated among alternative uses for the care of sickness, maintenance, and improvement of health.

questions.question: When blue litmus was added to an unknown liquid in a test tube, it turned red. What was the liquid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** acid.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acid**

 
 
• Acids are substances that have a sour taste, have one or more replaceable hydrogen atoms, and **turn blue litmus and methyl orange to red**.
 
• **Example:** Hydrochloric acid, nitric acid, sulphuric acid, etc.
 
 
 
• **Litmus**:
 
 
• It is an indicator that shows a color change in the solution as the **pH of the solution changes.**
 
• It is used to identify whether a solution is acidic, basic, or neutral.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water**

 
 
• It is vital for all known forms of life, even though it provides no calories or organic nutrients
 
• Its chemical formula is** H₂O.**
 
• A Ph of pure water is** 7.**
 
 
 
• **An alkali**
 
 
• Base or alkali turn red litmus to blue, methyl orange to yellow, and have a bitter taste.
 
• These solutions are soapy to touch.
 
• **Example: **Potassium Hydroxide, Magnesium Hydroxide, Sodium Hydroxide, etc.
 
 
 
• **Saline**
 
 
• Saline or salts are the compounds obtained by the reaction of acid and base, such reactions are called neutralization reactions.
 
• **Example: **Sodium Chloride, Potash alum, etc.

questions.question: Identify the unit of measurement of energy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Joule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Energy**

 
 
• Energy is measured as the capacity to do work.
 
• It is a scalar quantity.
 
• Its SI unit is **Joule** and CGS unit is** Erg.**
 
• There are different forms of energy:
 
 

 
• Heat Energy: It is the energy by a body due to its temperature.
 
• Internal Energy: The total energy possessed by a body by virtue of the particular configuration of its molecules and also their random motion is called internal energy.
 
• Electrical Energy: The energy required to maintain the flow of current in an electric appliance is called electrical energy.
 
• Chemical Energy: The energy absorbed or released during a chemical reaction is called chemical energy.
 
• Nuclear Energy: The energy absorbed or released during a nuclear reaction is called nuclear energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following devices is NOT used to enter data into a computer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Monitor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To enter data into a computer, an input device is required.
 
• **Input Device**: It can be defined as an electromechanical device that allows the user to enter data into the computer for analysis and storage and to give commands to the computer.
 
 
• **Example:** Keyboard, Mouse, Scanner, etc.
 
 
 
• **Output Device**: It is any piece of computer hardware equipment used to communicate the results of data carried out by an information processing to the outside world.
 
 
• **Example:** Monitor, Printer, Plotter, etc.
 
 
 
• **Monitor**
 
 
• It is an output device.
 
• It is also known as the Visual Display Unit.
 
• The monitor is provided along with the computer to view the display result.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Scanner**

 
 
• It is an optical input device and uses light as an input source to convert an image into an electronic form that can be stored on the computer.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard**
 
 
• It is one of the most common input devices.
 
• It is used to enter data or information, which may be in numeric form or alphabets form in a computer system.
 
 
 
• **Mouse**
 
 
• It is a small handheld device having two or three buttons on its upper side and also has a small wheel between the buttons which provides a means to input data and commands by selecting through moving an arrow.

questions.question: Which is the correct sequence of rulers of the Mughal Empire?

options.text: Babur, Humayun, Aurangzeb, Jhangir, Shahjahan, Bahadur, Shah, Akbar

Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shahjahan, Aurangzeb, Bahadur Shah

questions.question: Cirrus and cumulus are types of ______.

__
 
• **Clouds**

 
 
• Clouds help regulate Earth's temperature.
 
• They bring rain to different regions.
 
• Clouds develop out of the process of changing moisture from a gas to liquid through a process called convection.
 
• There are three forms of clouds
 
 

 
• **Cirrus:** curly or fibrous
 
• **Stratus:** sheets or layers
 
• **Cumulus: **Heaped or piled

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil**

 
 
• Soils are a complex mixture of water, air, minerals, and a number of organisms that are decaying.
 
• It forms at the surface of the land.
 
• It is the skin of the earth.
 
• It is capable of supporting plant life and is vital to life on earth.
 
• It is classified into four types:
 
 

 
• Sandy Soil
 
• Silt Soil
 
• Clay Soil
 
• Loamy Soil

 
• **Mountains**

 
 
• It is an elevated portion of the Earth's crust generally with steep sides.
 
• Forces inside and outside the earth manage the shape of the earth's surface.
 
• There are four types of mountains:
 
 

 
• Volcanic Mountains
 
• F old Mountains
 
• Block Mountain
 
• Residual Mountains

questions.question: What type of depositional topography is formed when water currents flowing from high levels are fragmented into low-sloping terrestrial sloping plains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alluvial Fans.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alluvial Fans**

 
 
• They are formed when water currents flow from higher levels break into foot slope plains of low gradient.
 
• Normally very coarse load is carried by streams flowing over mountains slopes.
 
• Alluvial Fans in humid areas show normally low cones with a gentle slope from head to down.
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 
 
• **Natural Embankment**
 
 
• It provides a gradual transition from land to water and takes nature and the landscape into account.
 
• It is not steep like traditional river banks.
 
 
 
• **Flood Plains**
 
 
• It is a flat area of land next to a river or stream.
 
• It stretches from the banks of the river to the outer edges of the valley.
 
 
 
• **Antiperspirant**
 
 
• It is a substance applied to the body to protect against sweat and odor.
 
• It is like deodorant.

questions.question: On which day of the year is the earth farthest from the sun, at a position called aphelion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 July**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Aphelion

 
 
• It is the point of Earth's orbit that is farthest from the Sun.
 
• When the earth reaches aphelion, the sun appears slightly smaller in the sky at any other time of year.
 
• The earth reaches aphelion only once a year.
 
• It happens near of 4th of July.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Perihelion

 
 
• ​It is the point of the Earth's orbit that is nearest to the Sun.
 
• It happens near of 4th of January.
 
• The earth reaches perihelion only once a year
 
 
 
• Equinox
 
 
• It refers to a day with an equal duration of day and night.
 
• There are two equinoxes in a year:
 
 

 
• March 20( Vernal Equinox)
 
• September 22( Autumnal Equinox)

 
• Solstice

 
 
• ​It is the time of the year when the sun is farthest from the equatorial giving the long days or nights.
 
• It happens twice a year
 

 
 
• Summer Solstice ( June 21)
 
• Winter Solstice( December 22)
 
 

c6

questions.question: Kartarpur Sahib corridor connects Dera Baba Nanak Shrine in Gurdaspur, India to Kartarpur Gurudwara in Pakistan, which is located near the banks of the river ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ravi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Guru Nanak, the first guru of Sikhism founded the Kartarpur on the bank of the Ravi River.
 
• The Kartarpur Sahib Corridor is 4.1 km. the passage that connects the Dera Baba Nanak shrine in Gurdaspur with the Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Kartarpur, Pakistan.
 
• The Kartarpur Sahib Corridor is established on 9 November 2019.
 
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Kartarpur Corridor and flagged off the first batch of over 500 Indian Pilgrims.
 
• **Ravi**
 
 
• It is one of the five rivers of the Indus System.
 
• The Ravi River originates in the Himalayas in the Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• Under the Indus Water Treaty of 1960, the waters of the Ravi are provided to India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sutlej**

 
 
• It is one of the six rivers of the Indus System.
 
• The Sutlej River originates from Mount Kailash.
 
• Under the Indus Water Treaty of 1960, the waters of the Ravi are provided to India.
 
• The Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on the river Sutlej.
 
 
 
• **Chenab**
 
 
• It is one of the six rivers of the Indus System.
 
• The Chenab River originates from Baralacha Pass.
 
• Under the Indus Water Treaty of 1960, the waters of the Ravi are provided to Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Jhelum**
 
 
• It is one of the six rivers of the Indus System.
 
• The Jhelum River originates from Pir Panjal Range
 
• Under the Indus Water Treaty of 1960, the waters of the Ravi are provided to Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Beas:**
 
 
• ​The Beas River is a river in north India. The river rises in the Himalayas in central Himachal Pradesh, India, and flows for some 470 kilometers to the Sutlej River in the state of Punjab.
 
• Its total length is 470 kilometers and its drainage basin is 20,303 square kilometers large.

questions.question: The President of India can hold office for a term of ______ year/s.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 years.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 56**__: The President shall hold the office for a period of years from the date on which he enters upon his office.
 
• **__Article 55__**: It deals with the manner of the election of the President.
 __
 
• The election of the President is done by the system of proportional representation by the means of the single transferable vote and the voting is done by secret ballot.
 
 
 
• **Article 54**__:The President shall be elected by the members of the electoral college consists of :
 __
 
• Elected members of both the houses of the Parliament.
 
• Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the states.
 
• Elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of the Union Territory having Legislative Assembly( National Capital Territory of Delhi and Puducherry).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• President__ 

 
 
• **Article 52:** There shall be a President of India.
 
• He is the constitutional head of the executive of India.
 
• The term of the office of the President is 5 years.
 
• He is the first citizen of India.
 
• He is an integral part of the Indian Parliament.
 
• He can submit his resignation to the Vice President of India.
 
• He is the supreme commander of the Indian Armed Forces
 
• First President of India: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
 
• Current President: Droupadi Murmu

• Bharat Ratna

 
 
• It is the highest civilian award of India.
 
• It was instituted in the year 1954.
 
• The first recipients of the Bharat Ratna were Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, C.Rajagopalachari, and C.V. Raman.
 
• The foreigner to receive to Bharat Ratna was Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan who was also known as Frontier Gandhi.
 
• Till now, it has been awarded to 48 individuals out of which 16 were awarded posthumously.
